## 维护者速读(席位终稿 · Head-sha: 486b6feb8f · 2026-11-17T19:47Z)

- 改了什么：技能文档 `data-hooks.md` 里「before 钩子」的事务一格，原来只写「在事务内」，现在讲清楚：钩子经 `ctx.api` 写的数据和外层保存同属一个事务，外层任何一处被拒，钩子的写入一起回滚，不能单独豁免;并列出四种不开事务的例外(调用方自己开了事务、对象不在默认数据源、默认驱动不支持事务如 turso 远程、代码注册的钩子)。另加一条「不要」：before 钩子不要经 `ctx.api` 往别的数据源写业务记录(会被拒，只有审计类账本例外)。配两条评测用例。
- 为什么改:#34412 已经让引擎这样工作(PR #34503),但给 AI 读的技能还写着旧说法，AI 会写出「以为能留下的日志写入」或「跨数据源写」的钩子，运行时才发现被回滚或被拒。
- 风险与回滚：只改技能文本和评测，不改任何运行代码;为不超 token 上限，删了同文件里四处重复表述，席位已逐条核对这些事实在同文件别处仍在。回滚即 revert。
- 先看:`skills/objectstack-data/references/data-hooks.md` 第 62 行(事务一格)与 Best Practices 的 DON'T 一条。
- 两分钟验证：打开该文件第 62 行，读 before 一列：应写明「同一事务、无单钩豁免、四种例外」。
- 需要你做的：批准本 PR(受管面 Tier H，席位不能自批);批准前还欠一次契约审核(L2),已请 l2-review#3。

席位意见：建议批准。四个例外与跨数据源拒绝都由开发对着引擎代码与现有测试逐条核过(MongoDB 一条保留「读自代码、未实测」),删掉的四处重复席位逐条复核仍在原文件。

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `486b6feb8f17a9bec275662aa0f9a5c6c9acfb7a`
Local-runs: none
Scope: skills/objectstack-data/references/data-hooks.md, skills/objectstack-data/evals/hooks-security-seeds-datasources.json + none
Security-touching: yes

PR #34964, card #34504, face `rules` (governed `skills/**`). Read: the card body and all six comments, the PR body and both PR comments, the net diff against `main` (three files), the 44 check-runs on this head. Code read on `origin/main` (`8b550f8193`), never reviewed: `packages/objectql/src/engine-hooks-and-functions.ts` (`opensAfterAbortUnit`, `registerHook` options), `engine-insert.ts` (unit entry, `enforceTransactionOrigin` call), `engine-execute-transactions.ts` (`enforceTransactionOrigin`), `engine.ts` (`SYSTEM_LEDGER_LIFECYCLE_CLASSES`), `engine-secrets-and-routing.ts` (`isSystemLedgerObject`, routing order), `transaction-errors.ts`, `engine-after-hook-abort-unit.test.ts` (pin titles), `packages/drivers/driver-turso/src/turso-driver.ts`, `packages/drivers/driver-mongodb/src/mongodb-driver.ts`, `packages/qa/scenarios/src/skill-evals/grade.ts`, `content/docs/automation/hooks.mdx`, `content/docs/api/data-flow.mdx`. The changeset is read for its level and declaration lines only.

Why `Security-touching: yes`: the path name does not show it, but two changed hunks sit on security teaching. (1) The pattern 4 hunk edits the "Data Masking on Read" callout: it removes the sentence that says one `afterFind` subscription covers `findOne`, which is the coverage of a read-masking control. (2) The new DON'T teaches that an `audit`-class ledger row is written outside the transaction and survives its rollback, which is audit-trail behaviour. Neither is wrong (see ④), but neither is plain wording either.

### ① Derived judgments

- Premise: holds. On the merge base (`fff0ad0c18`) the `before*` Transaction cell said "Within transaction". On `main` today it still does; nothing else has taught the rule in that cell.
- Every taught sentence was checked against the code on `main`, not against the PR body's table. Result in ④: all hold on their intended reading; one phrase has a second reading that is false (S1).
- `main` has moved since the base (`data-hooks.md` changed by other PRs, #35309 among them, and the eval file gained ids 27 to 31). Read with git plumbing only, no checkout: the three-way merge of this head onto `main` is textually clean, the merged eval ids are unique (25 and 26 are free on `main`), and the merged `data-hooks.md` is 40469 bytes, 10118 tokens against `main`'s ceiling of 10122. Headroom after the merge is 4 tokens, not the 19 the PR body reports for its own base.
- The four removed restatements: each fact still stands at this head and on the merged tree. `findOne` coverage: event table rows and the "Why so few?" note. Per-row `after*` dispatch, `previous` pre-image, `input.id` / `ctx.previous.id`: the "Why so few?" note ("Both phases dispatch once per matched row"). Declarative fields only on the bound path: Registration method 2, which is the more exact statement (`defineStack({ hooks })` or `ql.bindHooks`). Intro sentence: the page's own contents list.
- Gates: the check-runs on this head are the verdicts. 28 `success`, 16 `skipped` (opt-in, queue-only or path-filtered), none failed or pending. `Check Changeset`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `PR-body guards`, `Lint · docs & code guards` and `Lint · repo & tooling gates` are `success`. The dev's four locally unmeasured families ride those CI lanes.

### ② Semver level

`@objectstack/skills` `patch`, `Clause-②: no`, `Metadata-protocol: none`, the same pair in the PR body and the changeset body. Correct: the diff changes teaching text and eval fixtures, moves nothing an author can write, and `skills/**` ships in that package, so a changeset is owed and `skip-changeset` would be wrong. No `Clause-②` arm applies. `Check Changeset` is `success`.

### ③ Boundary flags

- `open_questions`: none in the dev report.
- Deviation, changeset outside the named `skills/**` surface: accepted, the publish rule requires it.
- Deviation, deletions on lines the card did not name (to pay the token ratchet): accepted. Each removal is a restatement, verified above; no ceiling moved.
- Deviation, "transaction" where the governing docs say "unit of work": accepted, it matches the rest of the page and the table row.
- Deviation, throwaway probe file: nothing of it is in the diff (three files).
- Out-of-scope finding, the `api.transaction` row: filed by the seat as #34967 per the card thread, and `main` now carries that row's fix (#35309: "Inside a unit already open ... it joins that unit"). It agrees with this PR's cell.
- Out-of-scope note, PostgreSQL no-savepoint: carrier #34563, not taught here. Accepted.
- SQL push-down (Prime Directive 5): the changed hunks teach no query pattern, no id materialisation and no in-app join. Nothing to flag.
- Author: the PR and its comments are by `objectstack-fleet[bot]`.

### ④ Design judgment

`data-hooks.md`, the `before*` Transaction cell, sentence by sentence against `opensAfterAbortUnit` on `main`:

- "One transaction with the outer write; a refusal anywhere in it rolls back the hook's `ctx.api` writes too": holds. `sideWriting` is true for any metadata-bound `before*` entry on the same verb that matches the object, and `insert` / `update` / `delete` re-enter through `inAfterAbortUnit`. Pinned for a declared validation (insert, update) and a later `beforeDelete` hook.
- "no per-hook opt-out": holds. `sideWriting` reads neither `onError` nor `async`. The only switch is the caller's `skipAutomations`, under which the hook does not run at all.
- "a transaction the caller opened decides": holds (first line of the function; pinned).
- "a default driver with no transactions (turso's remote transport) opens none, so those writes stay stored": holds (`driverSupportsTransactions`; `transactionsUnsupported: this.transportMode === 'remote'`; pinned).
- "a hook registered in code (`registerHook`) opens none": holds for `registerHook` without `meta`, which is what the page's own method 2 shows. The page rightly does not attach "stay stored" here: a unit another hook on the object opened would still cover it.
- "MongoDB needs a replica set (read in code, not measured)": the driver's `beginTransaction` always calls `session.startTransaction()` and declares no `transactionsUnsupported`. The hedge is honest and is the one the card asks for.
- "an object off the default datasource ... opens none, so those writes stay stored": true of the object the HOOK is on (`this.getDriver(object) === defaultDriver`, where `object` is the outer write's). See S1.

The DON'T: holds. Inside the unit, `enforceTransactionOrigin` throws `CrossDatasourceTransactionWriteError` for a non-ledger object on another driver, at the top of the side write; a ledger class object on another datasource runs outside the unit and survives. In the three no-unit exits the write is not refused but stored, so the advice "don't" is right on every path.

Evals 25 and 26: both discriminate (a model without the new text names neither `registerHook` nor the error class), and the scenario order in 25 is the pinned one (hook write, then the declared validation refuses). Eval 26's remedy matches `hooks.mdx` ("Keep the objects a `before*` hook writes on the default datasource").

S1 (should-fix) — "an object off the default datasource" does not say WHICH object, and one reading is false. In the cell, the only objects in view are the ones the hook writes through `ctx.api`, so the natural reading is "a write to an object off the default datasource opens no transaction and stays stored after a refusal". The runtime does the opposite: with the hooked object on the default datasource, that write is refused with `CrossDatasourceTransactionWriteError` and nothing is stored. This is the exact mistake the card exists to prevent ("rely on a log-the-attempt write surviving a refusal"), and the DON'T 740 lines later then reads as a contradiction instead of a rule. Eval 25's `expected_output` repeats it with two objects in play ("the object is off the default datasource": `time_entry` or `timesheet`?), so the reference answer has a false reading too. Fix: name the hooked object in both places, for example "the hook's object off the default datasource" in the cell and "`time_entry` is off the default datasource" in eval 25. Mind the budget: after a rebase on `main` the file has 4 tokens (16 bytes) of headroom.

Nits (no effect on correctness or the contract; fix with S1 or leave as accepted deviation):

- N1 — the DON'T's ledger clause is true only for a ledger on another datasource; an `audit`-class object that stays on the default datasource rolls back with the save. The sentence's scope ("to another datasource") carries it and eval 26 says it outright.
- N2 — after the merge with `main` the page names the same refusal two ways: `CrossDatasourceTransactionWriteError` here, `400 ERR_CROSS_DATASOURCE_TRANSACTION_WRITE` in the `api.transaction` row (#35309). Both are real (class name and `code`).
- N3 — eval assertions: 25 requires `registerHook` although its prompt's hook is declared in the stack, so a correct answer that lists only the two stay-stored setups fails; the grader is a case-sensitive substring match, so "Default datasource" at a sentence start fails both cases; 26 has no `must_not_contain`, so an answer that writes the hook and merely mentions the error passes. The runner is not a gate.
- N4 — "turso's" is lower-case; the skill elsewhere writes `driver-turso` or "Turso".

No must-fix. One should-fix (S1): a delta review of the new head is owed by this reviewer before the maintainer's approval is sought. Tier H stands either way.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `314d9cc0ca914b6315d7d12c8a8e4d710c20b625`
Local-runs: none
Scope: skills/objectstack-data/references/data-hooks.md, skills/objectstack-data/evals/hooks-security-seeds-datasources.json + none
Security-touching: yes

Delta round on record 7002617585 (head `486b6feb8f`), which left S1 open. PR #34964, card #34504, face `rules` (governed `skills/**`). Read: the card body and its seven comments (delta report 7002915160 among them), the PR body, file list and six comments, the delta `486b6feb8f..314d9cc0ca` on `skills` and `.changeset`, the net diff against `origin/main` (`35c6331094`), and the 45 check-runs on this head. Code read on `origin/main`, never reviewed: `packages/objectql/src/engine-hooks-and-functions.ts` (`opensAfterAbortUnit`), `engine-hook-dispatch.ts` (`inAfterAbortUnit`), `engine-execute-transactions.ts` (`enforceTransactionOrigin`), `engine-after-hook-abort-unit.test.ts` (pin titles), `packages/drivers/driver-turso/src/turso-driver.ts`, `content/docs/automation/hooks.mdx`. The changeset is read for its level, its declaration lines and its agreement with the page.

`Security-touching: yes`, restated on this head: the net diff still edits the "Data Masking on Read" callout (it removes the sentence on `findOne` coverage of an `afterFind` mask) and the new DON'T still teaches that an `audit`-class ledger row is written outside the transaction and survives its rollback. This round changed neither hunk.

### ① Derived judgments

- The delta is two commits: a merge of `origin/main` `35c6331094` (`cfeb6462d1`) and the S1 wording (`314d9cc0ca`). The PR's own change this round is three one-line edits: the `before*` Transaction cell, eval 25's `expected_output`, and the changeset paragraph.
- The merge is clean. `git diff origin/main 314d9cc0ca` names exactly the PR's three files (+43 −18), so the head is `main` plus this PR and nothing else. The merged eval ids are 1 to 31, each once; 25 and 26 are this PR's.
- The merge leaves the taught sentences true. `main` now carries the `api.transaction` row from #35309 ("Inside a unit already open (the one the hook's write runs in, or a caller's) it joins that unit") and eval 28 ("a plain `ctx.api` write to it inside the save's unit is refused the same way"). Both agree with this PR's cell and its DON'T.
- The four removed restatements still stand on the merged page: `findOne` coverage (event table rows and the "Why so few?" note), per-row dispatch (same note), the declarative fields on the bound path only (Registration method 2, `ql.bindHooks`), and the page's contents list.
- Budget: the merged page is 888 lines, 40467 bytes, measured from the tree. The dev reports 10117 tokens against a ceiling of 10122. I did not measure tokens (read-only round); the ratchet's verdict is the `Lint · docs & code guards` run, which was still in progress when I read it.
- Gates, as read at the end of this round: 45 check-runs; 21 `success`, 18 `skipped`, 6 `in_progress`, none failed. `Check Changeset` (both runs), `PR-body guards` (both runs), `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `Lint · ESLint`, `Lint · PM dispatch-gates`, `Type Check · workspace`, `Type Check · source gates` and `Build Core` are `success`. Still running: `Lint · docs & code guards`, `Lint · repo & tooling gates`, `Lint · CI, release & engine gates`, `Type Check · consumer gates`, `Test Core (1/10)`, `Test Core (2/10)`. Their conclusions are the gate verdicts; this record does not stand in for them.

### ② Semver level

`@objectstack/skills` `patch`, `Clause-②: no`, `Metadata-protocol: none`, the same pair in the PR body and the changeset. Unchanged this round and still correct: teaching text and eval fixtures only, nothing an author can write moves, and `skills/**` ships in that package. No `Clause-②` arm applies. `Check Changeset` is `success` on this head.

### ③ Boundary flags

- `open_questions`: none in the delta report.
- Deviation, two phrases the earlier record read as holding were reworded to pay for "hooked": read in ④, both hold.
- Deviation, the changeset text was edited: it is this PR's own new changeset and now matches the page. Accepted.
- Deviation, two derived gate families not measured locally: they ride CI.
- Earlier flags (changeset outside `skills/**`, deletions on lines the card did not name, "transaction" for "unit of work", the `api.transaction` row now taught by #35309, PostgreSQL no-savepoint on carrier #34563): unchanged, accepted as in record 7002617585.
- SQL push-down (Prime Directive 5): the changed hunks teach no query pattern, no id materialisation and no in-app join. Nothing to flag.

### ④ Design judgment

The `before*` Transaction cell on this head, the three changed phrases against `opensAfterAbortUnit` on `main`:

- "a hooked object off the default datasource ... opens none, so those writes stay stored after a refusal": holds, and it now has one reading. The function's last line is `this.getDriver(object) === defaultDriver`, where `object` is the outer write's object, the one the hook matched. With that object off the default driver no unit is opened, so the hook's `ctx.api` writes are not covered and stay stored. The false reading S1 named (a write TO an off-default object stays stored) is no longer available: the phrase names the object the hook is on, and the object a hook writes to is not "hooked". The DON'T further down now reads as a separate rule and not as a contradiction.
- "a caller's open transaction decides": holds. The first line of the function returns `false` when a threaded handle is open (a closed handle is not open, `isClosedUnitHandle`) or an ambient unit is in the store; the write then runs in that unit and its owner commits or rolls back. Pinned: "CONTROL inside a caller-opened transaction() — it joins (one unit), and the caller decides". "open" is the right word and loses nothing against "a transaction the caller opened".
- "rolls back the hook's `ctx.api` writes" (the word "too" dropped): holds. The sentence still names the refusal's own scope ("a refusal anywhere in it"), and the row of the refused write is rolled back by the same unit; "too" carried no fact.
- "Turso's remote transport": `transactionsUnsupported: this.transportMode === 'remote'` on `main`. Unchanged in substance.

Eval 25, `expected_output`: "`time_entry`, the hooked object, is off the default datasource" names which of the two objects in the prompt is meant, and it is the one the code tests. The prompt and the assertions are unchanged. Eval 26 is unchanged.

The changeset paragraph carries the same two phrases as the page. It keeps "writes too" in its own sentence, which is prose about the change and true.

Findings by id:

- S1: closed. The cell and eval 25 name the hooked object; read against the code above.
- N1: open, accepted. The ledger clause in the DON'T is unchanged; its scope ("to another datasource") still carries it and eval 26 says it outright.
- N2: open, accepted. On the merged page the refusal is named by class (`CrossDatasourceTransactionWriteError`, the DON'T) and by code (`400 ERR_CROSS_DATASOURCE_TRANSACTION_WRITE`, the `api.transaction` row). Both are real.
- N3: open, accepted. Eval 25 and 26 assertions are unchanged; the runner is not a gate.
- N4: closed. "Turso's" is capitalised in the cell, eval 25 and the changeset.
- N5 (nit, new): the PR body is stale against this head in two places a reader acts on. "What changes", item 1, still quotes the old cell verbatim ("a transaction the caller opened decides; an object off the default datasource ... turso's"). The two-minute verification line still expects `9992 tokens (ceiling 10011; headroom 19)`, where the dev's reading on this head is `10117 tokens (ceiling 10122; headroom 5)`. The tree is right and the Acceptance note at the top of that section does carry the new cell; the delta report lists the body edits under `pr_body_changes`. No effect on the contract.

No must-fix, no should-fix.

Tier H stands: the maintainer's approval is owed, and the six check-runs still in progress must conclude before landing.
